dva-med-037.text: A developer read that Amazon S3 offers strong consistency (strong read-after-write) for all operations. What this guarantees in practice for the application?
options: That objects are replicated to all regions instantly
That two clients can never write on the same object
After one PUT successful (new or overwritten), any subsequent reading returns the latest version of the object — no old data window
That the S3 began to support multi-object transactions
dva-med-037.explanation: Since 2020 o S3 is strongly consistent: GET/LIST after writing immediately reflect the current state, eliminating the old windows of eventual consistency in overwritten and listages.
dva-med-037.hint: He wrote, read: what comes back is always the last version — without 'eco' of the past.
optionRationales: Since 2020 o S3 is strongly consistent: GET/LIST after writing immediately reflect the current state, eliminating the old windows of eventual consistency in overwritten and listages.
Competing writings are still possible (last win) — reading consistency is not writing block.
Strong consistency within the Bucket Region — replication between Regions is a separate and asynchronous resource.
There are no transactions between objects in S3 — the guarantee is about reading reflect the latest writing of the CADA object.

dva-med-038.text: A serverless application uses several functions Lambda which need common logic of structured logging, metrics and tracking with little repeated code. In addition to layers, which official library AWS accelerates these good practices in function Lambda?
options: AWS Lambda Powertools (Python/TypeScript/Java/.NET), with ready-made structured logging utilities, metrics EMF and tracing
Amazon WorkDocs SDK
AWS Amplify CLI
AWS IoT Greengrass
dva-med-038.explanation: Powertools standardizes observability and good practices (structured logger, built-in metrics, X-ray plotting, idempotence) with decorators/middlewares — reducing boilerplate code between functions.
dva-med-038.hint: The official electrical tools of the Lambda: logger, metrics and plot ready to plug.
optionRationales: Powertools standardizes observability and good practices (structured logger, built-in metrics, X-ray plotting, idempotence) with decorators/middlewares — reducing boilerplate code between functions.
Amplify accelerates full-stack apps (front + backend) — is not the library of observability utilities for functions.
WorkDocs deals with document collaboration — no relationship with standards Lambda.
Greengrass takes computer to the edge IoT — is not toolkit of good serverless practices.

dva-med-039.text: An endpoint needs to serve a real-time leaderboard with the 10 top scorers of a game, updated to each score. Which data structure of Redis (ElastiCache) solves this ranking with native sorting operations?
options: Sorted Set (ZADD/ZRANGE), that keeps members sorted by score automatically
A common set (SADD)
A list (LPUSH) with the scores
A string JSON with the full array reordered to each writing
dva-med-039.explanation: The sorted set is the classic leaderboard structure: inserts/updates with ZADD keep the ordination by score, and ZRANGE/ZREVRANGE returns the top in O(log N) — without manual rearrangement.
dva-med-039.hint: The structure of the Redis made for podiums: set 'ordered by points'.
optionRationales: The sorted set is the classic leaderboard structure: inserts/updates with ZADD keep the ordination by score, and ZRANGE/ZREVRANGE returns the top in O(log N) — without manual rearrangement.
Serializing and reordering everything at each point loses native operations and creates running conditions.
Lists preserve INSERTION order — do not order by score.
Sets ensure uniqueness without ordering — no ranking per score.

dva-med-040.text: An application saves on DynamoDB and need to decide between possibly consistent and strongly consistent readings. What is the trade-off between the two options in a Query/GetItem?
options: Strongly consistent readings are free to encourage your use
Possible consistent readings can return data from another table

Strongly consistent readings guarantee the most recent data, but cost twice as much reading capacity and have slightly higher latency; possibly consistent (standard) readings cost half and can reflect data lags for moments
There is no practical difference; the terms are only historical
dva-med-040.explanation: The DynamoDB snake 1 RCU by highly consistent reading of up to 4 KB against 0,5 RCU if necessary: the choice balances the data fresh against cost and latency — possible readings are sufficient for most cases.
dva-med-040.hint: Guaranteed freshness costs twice as much RCU; the read 'relaxed' is half rate with possible delay of moments.
optionRationales: The DynamoDB snake 1 RCU by highly consistent reading of up to 4 KB against 0,5 RCU if necessary: the choice balances the data fresh against cost and latency — possible readings are sufficient for most cases.
It's the opposite: strong consistency consumes twice as much reading capacity.
The possible consistency refers to the ATRASO internal replication of the same table — never to different table data.
The difference is real at cost (2x), latency and freshness — and configurable by call with the ConsistentRead parameter.

dva-med-041.text: An application needs to encrypt files from 100 MB before recording them, but to API Encryption of KMS accepted at the most 4 KB of data per call. Which standard solves large data encryption with key KMS?
options: Request an increase in the limit of 4 KB via support
Encryption Envelope: Use GenerateDataKey to get a data key, encrypt the file locally with it and store the encrypted version of the data key next to the file
Divide the file into 25.600 blocks of 4 KB and call Encrypt for each
Store the file without encryption, because the KMS does not support large data
dva-med-041.explanation: Encryption envelope is the standard of KMS for large data: the data key encrypts the file locally (fast), and only the data key itself — small — is protected by the key KMS; in the reading, the Decrypt of the key data unlocked the file.
dva-med-041.hint: The big key protects a small key; the small key protects the big file — all inside an envelope'.
optionRationales: Encryption envelope is the standard of KMS for large data: the data key encrypts the file locally (fast), and only the data key itself — small — is protected by the key KMS; in the reading, the Decrypt of the key data unlocked the file.
Thousands of calls per file would be slow and expensive — the limit of 4 KB exists just to induce the envelope pattern.
The limit of the API is not adjustable — is a service design feature.
The KMS supports any size via encryption envelope — giving up protection is not option.

dva-med-042.text: By compliance policy, TODO object recorded in a pocket S3 must use encryption SSE-KMS with a specific key — uploads that do not meet this need to be rejected at the time.?
options: Bucket policy with condition that denies PutObject when the encryption headers do not specify aws:kms (and the expected key)
Enable versioning to encrypt old versions
Trust that developers will always pass the right headers
Rolling a night job that excludes objects without encryption
dva-med-042.explanation: A Bucket policy with Deny conditioned to the headers s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption rejects uploads out of the pattern itself API — the imposition happens in the resource, regardless of the customer.
dva-med-042.hint: Bucket doorman may require 'seal' KMS' in the heading — without a stamp, the PUT nor does it come in.
optionRationales: A Bucket policy with Deny conditioned to the headers s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption rejects uploads out of the pattern itself API — the imposition happens in the resource, regardless of the customer.
Discipline without fail force — compliance requires technical blocking of the resource.
Later cleaning leaves non-compliant data exposed for hours and destroys them instead of rejecting at source.
Version preserves versions — does not apply or require encryption.

dva-med-043.text: An application allows navigation as a guest (no login) with reading access to a public catalog newsletter, and extended access after login. Amazon Cognito supports credentials AWS separate for authenticated and un authenticated users?
options: Distribute user key accesses IAM 'guest no app
Identity Pools with unauthenticated identities enabled, mapping roles IAM different for guests and authenticated
Cognito does not support access without login
User Pools with fictional users called 'guest''
dva-med-043.explanation: The Identity Pool issues temporary credentials on two tracks: the guest role (minimum permissions) and the authenticated role (expanded permissions) — the standard for guest experience + login.
dva-med-043.hint: The 'identity pool' has two stripes: one roller for visitors, another for those who checked in.
optionRationales: The Identity Pool issues temporary credentials on two tracks: the guest role (minimum permissions) and the authenticated role (expanded permissions) — the standard for guest experience + login.
Shared false accounts destroy audit and security — guest support is native to Identity Pool.
Static keys embedded in apps are removable — classic vulnerability that temporary credentials eliminate.
Unauthenticated identities are an explicit feature of Identity Pools.

dva-med-044.text: A web application wants to delegate the login, registration and MFA to Cognito, using OAuth flow 2.0 of authorization code to receive tokens safely. Cognito provides these ready screens and OAuth endpoints?
options: User Pool's Hosted UI with Own Domain and OAuth Endpoints 2.0 (authorize/token) supporting the authorization grant code
Build the screens from scratch and send the passwords to API of the IAM
AWS WAF with embedded login page
CloudFront Functions generating login forms
dva-med-044.explanation: Hosted UI delivers managed authentication pages (login, registration), MFA, social) and implements standard OAuth streams — the app receives code and tokens exchange at the endpoint /token.
dva-med-044.hint: The Cognito 'hosts the login interface for you — with the classic OAuth endpoints behind.
optionRationales: Hosted UI delivers managed authentication pages (login, registration), MFA, social) and implements standard OAuth streams — the app receives code and tokens exchange at the endpoint /token.
The IAM does not authenticate end users — and build everything manually reintroduces the work and risks that Hosted UI eliminates.
The WAF filter requests — does not provide interface or authentication flow.
Edge functions handle light requests — do not implement a full IdP with OAuth.

dva-med-045.text: One API no API Gateway needs custom permission: validate a owner token (no JWT of Cognito) consulting business rules before releasing each call. API Gateway executes this custom logic?
options: Native Authorizer of Cognito User Pool
One Lambda authorizer, who receives token, performs custom validation and returns the policy IAM allowing or denying the call
Validation within each backend function
API keys with use plans
dva-med-045.explanation: The Lambda Authorizer injects its own logic into the authorization: validates token against any rule/service and returns Allow/Deny (with context), with optional cache of the result — the path to out-of-standard schemes Cognito/IAM.
dva-med-045.hint: When the badge is 'out of standard', a function of yours turns door security — returning the access policy.
optionRationales: The Lambda Authorizer injects its own logic into the authorization: validates token against any rule/service and returns Allow/Deny (with context), with optional cache of the result — the path to out-of-standard schemes Cognito/IAM.
API keys measure and limit consumption — do not perform logical validation of owners tokens.
The Authorizer of Cognito validates only JWTs issued by the pool — tokens owners require custom authorizer.
Validate in the backend repeats code on each route and processes unauthorized requests — the bar authorizer before.

dva-med-046.text: A fintech hires a consulting firm that will need to assume a role in the fintech account. To avoid the problem of 'confused deputy' — where a third party is induced to use their access for the benefit of another customer — which element should be required in the trust policy of the roll?
options: A key KMS shared between accounts
An External ID agreed between the parties, validated in the condition sts:ExternalId of AssumeRole
A password shared by e-mail monthly
Temporary root access for consulting
dva-med-046.explanation: The External ID is the secret identifier that the third party must present when assuming the role: it prevents another consulting client from inducing him to use the access improperly — the classic mitigation of the confused deputy.
dva-med-046.hint: The 'secret contract code' that the third party needs to present when knocking on the roller door.
optionRationales: The External ID is the secret identifier that the third party must present when assuming the role: it prevents another consulting client from inducing him to use the access improperly — the classic mitigation of the confused deputy.
Passwords exchanged by informal channels do not integrate with AssumeRole nor offer conditional validation of the External ID.
Root is never granted to third parties — it violates all the security principles of the account.
Keys KMS protect data — do not authenticate AssumeRole's relationship of trust.

dva-med-047.text: The security team wants every Docker image sent to Amazon ECR is automatically verified against known vulnerabilities (CVEs) in their layers and packages. What resource meets this?
options: Trust that official base images never have vulnerabilities
Image scanning of ECR (basic or enhanced via Amazon Inspector), with push scan and continuous
AWS Shield Advanced in registration
Amazon Macie analyzing the image repository
dva-med-047.explanation: The ECR offers scan on push and, in enhanced mode with Inspector, continuous scan of images against VEC bases — findings appear per image with severity to block unsafe promotions.
dva-med-047.hint: The port inspects every container that docks — and can re-inspect the fleet when new threats arise.
optionRationales: The ECR offers scan on push and, in enhanced mode with Inspector, continuous scan of images against VEC bases — findings appear per image with severity to block unsafe promotions.
The Macie discover sensitive data in buckets S3 — does not sweep layers of container images.
Shield DDoS mitigation — does not analyze image content.
Official images receive CVEs constantly — continuous scanning exists because yesterday's base may be vulnerable today.

dva-med-048.text: A website distributes private videos via CloudFront and you need to authorize the access of subscribers: sometimes to a ONE file (individual link), sometimes to TODO the catalog (cents of URLs) without generating a link per file. CloudFront respond to each case, respectively?
options: Signed cookies for a file and signed URLs for the entire catalog
Signed URLs to authorize an individual file and signed cookies to release multiple content without changing URLs
Make the public-origin pocket with random names
Block by country with geo-restriction
dva-med-048.explanation: Signed URL implements the authorisation for a specific resource; the signed cookies send the authorisation in the browser and apply for a set of content — the classic private content pair in the CloudFront.
dva-med-048.hint: One ticket per movie (URL signed) or the entire festival bracelet (signed cookies)).
optionRationales: Signed URL implements the authorisation for a specific resource; the signed cookies send the authorisation in the browser and apply for a set of content — the classic private content pair in the CloudFront.
It's reversed.: URL signed is by resource; cookies cover the set without rewriting each link.
Darkness is not allowed — links leak and content is open.
Geographical restriction filters by origin — not authentic individual subscribers.
